notes: Panel has 7 core/secondary Y markers (RPS4Y1 DDX3Y EIF1AY KDM5D UTY ZFY USP9Y) plus XIST at core tier. XIST is positive inactive-X evidence only - XIST-negative is not male evidence (XCI erosion in hESC/hiPSC, XIST loss in tumours), and Y-low XIST-negative blood may be loss-of-Y rather than female.
Panel has 8 core/secondary Y markers (Ddx3y Eif2s3y Kdm5d Uty Usp9y Uba1y Zfy1 Zfy2) plus Xist at core tier. Mouse has no useful Rps4y1 or Eif1ay orthologue, so do not port the human panel by symbol.

4 core/secondary Y markers (EIF1AY DDX3Y ZFY USP9Y) plus an UNNAMED X-linked lncRNA at ENSBTAG00000070614 recovered by coordinate overlap as the probable XIST orthologue - it has no gene symbol, so match it by gene_id. Freemartin heifers are blood chimeras with their male twin, so bovine blood can be Y-positive from an animal correctly recorded as female.

Male-detector only: 7 core/secondary Y markers, no XIST orthologue in Ensembl 116. Marmosets are routinely haematopoietic chimeras with their dizygotic twin, so blood and marrow can genuinely carry both sexes.

Male-detector only: 7 core/secondary Y markers recovered from a vestigial 18-gene Y, and no XIST orthologue in Ensembl 116; female verdicts unsupported. Vero cells derive from this species and are female with a heavily rearranged genome.

Somatic sex is the X:autosome ratio through Sxl, NOT the Y: XO flies are sterile males and XXY flies are female, so no Y marker reaches core or secondary tier and Y expression must not drive the verdict. There is no X inactivation - the single male X is UPREGULATED by the MSL complex. The three usable markers are male-specific with the OPPOSITE polarity to XIST: roX1 (FBgn0019661), roX2 (FBgn0019660) and Sxl (FBgn0264270). Ensembl spells the lncRNAs lncRNA:roX1 and lncRNA:roX2, so match by gene_id.

Female-detector only, the mirror image of the male-detector species: F.catus_Fca126_mat1.0 is a maternal haplotype assembly with no Y, so there are zero Y markers, but an UNNAMED X-linked lncRNA at ENSFCTG00005010135 gives positive inactive-X evidence. Male verdicts unsupported. ID prefix changed from ENSFCAG to ENSFCTG with this assembly - accept both.

Female is the heterogametic sex, so W expression is FEMALE evidence and the mammalian polarity inverts. Exactly one W marker survives at secondary tier: ENSGALG00010011988, which Ensembl 116 names HINTLA1 - the classic names HINTW, ASW and Wpkci are synonyms only and will NOT match the panel, so match by gene_id. Z dosage compensation is incomplete and gene- and tissue-specific (male:female Z median around 1.4), so Z dosage supports but never decides.
Male-detector only: 7 core/secondary Y markers but no XIST orthologue annotated in Ensembl 116; female verdicts unsupported, absence of Y returns uncertain.
Male-detector only: 4 core/secondary Y markers (UTY ZFY USP9Y DDX3Y), no XIST orthologue in Ensembl 116; female verdicts unsupported.

Male-detector only, and a thin one: just 3 core/secondary Y markers (ZFY USP9Y KDM5D) survive filtering, and no XIST orthologue in Ensembl 116.

No heteromorphic sex chromosomes: sex is decided by the male-determining factor Nix inside a small M locus on chromosome 1, homomorphic with its m counterpart. Chromosome-level dosage carries no sex signal.

ZW with female heterogamety, but CAU_duck1.0 has Z and NO W chromosome, so the panel has zero W markers and only Z dosage remains. Ensembl models this as the subspecies Anas platyrhynchos platyrhynchos, taxid 8840.
XY male heterogamety on a pair of microchromosomes that AnoCar2.0 does not assemble as X or Y; the X is largely unassigned scaffold sequence.

No panel built. Heteromorphic XY with male heterogamety, but AgamP4 has X and no Y chromosome. Sex determination runs through Yob on the Y and dsx splicing, neither captured by a chromosome-level panel.

Haplodiploid: males are haploid from unfertilised eggs and females diploid, decided by heterozygosity at the csd locus. No sex chromosomes exist; the signal is ploidy plus a genotype, neither visible in a normalised expression matrix.

Hermaphrodite flowers, no sex chromosomes. Full ID fingerprint is ^AT[1-5CM]G[0-9]{5}$; only AT1G is registered because a bare AT prefix collides with human symbols (ATM, ATF4, ATP5F1A). Plants are refused because we have no curated per-species model, not because plants lack sex chromosomes - Silene, Cannabis, Populus and Asparagus have real XY or ZW systems.

ZW with female heterogamety, but the determinant is the W-derived Fem piRNA silencing Z-linked Masc, with Bmdsx sex-specific splicing downstream - HINTW is avian and has no silkworm orthologue. A piRNA is not polyadenylated, so polyA mRNA-seq may not capture it; the 211 W rows in the panel are unnamed repeat-region genes at inventory tier. Ensembl Metazoa uses RefSeq LOC* gene IDs with no species-distinctive prefix.

No Y chromosome exists: XX are hermaphrodites, XO are males. Sex is set by the X:autosome ratio, but the dosage compensation complex then halves X transcription in XX, so X expression does NOT separate XX from XO in RNA. Standard selfing cultures are overwhelmingly XX, so bulk RNA measures culture composition rather than sex. The panel is 6022 X-inventory rows and nothing else.
ROS_Cfam_1.0 yields only 2 unnamed Y genes, neither reaching core or secondary tier, and no XIST orthologue in Ensembl 116; there is no usable evidence in either direction.

Panel build FAILED: sex chromosomes are not assembled to named sequences in Ensembl 116 ARS1, so no X or Y rows exist. A future Ensembl release with a chromosome-level goat assembly would pick this up.
Panel build FAILED: Cavpor3.0 is scaffold-level and sex chromosomes are not assembled to named sequences in Ensembl 116.

ZW with female heterogamety, but Coturnix_japonica_2.0 yields only 5 W genes (AKAP8 AKAP8L WIZ and two unnamed), none reaching core or secondary tier and none W-specific in the HINTW sense; Z dosage alone is not decisive in birds.

The Ensembl 116 gene set yields X inventory only - no Y and no XIST orthologue. The chromosome-level CriGri-PICRH-1.0 assembly has an X but still no Y. CHO lines are female-derived and karyotypically unstable regardless.

Common laboratory strains (AB, TU) have lost the differentiated sex chromosome and determine sex polygenically with a strong environmental component; wild and natural strains DO carry WZ/ZZ sex linkage on chromosome 4. The correct statement is strain-dependent, not that zebrafish lack sex chromosomes - and a counts matrix does not reveal the strain.

Environmental sex determination: males and females are genetically identical clones and sex is induced by photoperiod, crowding and juvenile hormone. There is no genetic sex to call, yet the archive labels 2501 Daphnia samples Male or Female.
EquCab3.0 has X but no Y chromosome and no annotated XIST orthologue; the panel is X inventory only.

Bacteria have no sex. F+/F- conjugative fertility is plasmid-borne gene transfer, not genetic sex, and is where the male/female language in the metadata comes from. Locus tags are b#### which is far too generic to register as a detection prefix.
XY with a young, only partly degenerate Y that the reference does not assemble separately; sex-determination systems differ between Gasterosteus populations and sister species.
gorGor4 has X but no Y chromosome and no annotated XIST orthologue; the panel is X inventory only. Ensembl models this genome as the subspecies Gorilla gorilla gorilla, taxid 9595.
Naked_mole-rat_maternal is a female assembly: X present, no Y, and no annotated XIST orthologue; the panel is X inventory only.
Macaca_fascicularis_6.0 has X but no Y chromosome, so the panel has zero Y markers, and no XIST orthologue is annotated in Ensembl 116; no signal in either direction.
No panel built. ZW with female heterogamety, but Turkey_5.1 annotates only a handful of W genes. Turkeys also undergo spontaneous parthenogenesis, producing ZZ males from unfertilised eggs.
Panel build FAILED: MesAur1.0 is scaffold-level and sex chromosomes are not assembled to named sequences in Ensembl 116.
No panel built: MicOch1.0 has X but no Y chromosome. Several Microtus species have giant heterochromatic sex chromosomes and unusual XCI, so do not generalise across the genus.

Marsupial XCI is imprinted paternal-X silencing driven by the lncRNA RSX, and XIST does not exist in metatherians at all - but RSX is NOT in Ensembl 116, which still serves monDom5 (NCBI has RSX only on the newer mMonDom1.v assembly), and the opossum assembly has no Y. The panel is X inventory only, so marsupial support cannot work as specified.
No panel built: MusPutFur1.0 is scaffold-level with no chromosome assignment.

XY with a young, near-homomorphic sex chromosome and a gdf6 Y ALLELE as determiner - the signal is allelic, not presence or absence of a gene, so an expression matrix cannot see it. Sex determination also varies between strains.

Male determination is sdY, mobile and absent from the reference annotation, as in Atlantic salmon. Farmed stocks are frequently all-female or sex-reversed neomales, so recorded sex and genetic sex legitimately differ.

Monotreme five-pair X1Y1-X5Y5 translocation chain, bird-like at one end of the chain, no XIST, and partial gene-by-gene dosage compensation. Ensembl mOrnAna1.p.v1 carries X1-X5 and no Y. Not modelled.
OryCun2.0 has X but no Y chromosome and no annotated XIST orthologue; the panel is X inventory only.

Genuine XY with the male determiner dmrt1bY (DMY), a dmrt1 duplicate inside a small Y-specific region absent from the HdrR reference assembly. The rest of the Y is homomorphic with the X, so there is no panel and no dosage signal.
No panel built: panpan1.1 has X but no Y chromosome and no annotated XIST orthologue.
No panel built: Susie_PABv2 has X but no Y chromosome and no annotated XIST orthologue.

No sex chromosomes and no genetic sex. MATa/MATalpha mating type is a real and detectable feature at the MAT locus but it is not sex and is out of scope. Systematic gene IDs match ^Y[A-P][LR][0-9]{3}[WC] which is too generic to register as a detection prefix.

Male determination is sdY, a transposon-like mobile cassette that has jumped to different chromosomes in different populations and is absent from the reference annotation. Chromosome-level panels carry no sex signal in salmonids.

No sex chromosomes and no genetic sex; h+/h- mating type at mat1 is not sex. Gene IDs match ^SP[ABC][CPRT][0-9]+ but a bare SP prefix collides with human symbols (SPTBN1, SPARC, SPACA1), so no prefix is registered and detection is name-based.

ZW with female heterogamety, but bTaeGut1_v1.p has Z and NO W chromosome, so the panel has zero W markers and only Z dosage remains, which in birds is incompletely compensated and not decisive. Zebra finch also carries a germline-restricted chromosome absent from somatic tissue.
No panel built: turTru1 is scaffold-level with no chromosome assignment.

ZW with female heterogamety driven by the W-linked DM-W, a truncated dmrt1 paralogue. The genome is allotetraploid with L and S subgenomes, DM-W sits in a tiny W region, and gene IDs are in practice Xenbase XB-GENE-* or NCBI LOC* rather than an Ensembl prefix.
Sex determination is polymorphic between lines, with W, Z and Y chromosomes segregating within the same species and no fixed heteromorphic pair; DM-W is absent. No panel is defensible.
